analysis: Integrated both units. The PR adds Swift Autopilot changes plus docs. (1) The Autopilot set widens to every verified cached catalog build, capped at 256 IDs, with no new consent step. (2) Coordinator-driven downloads via prefetch_model are default-on with saved consent, a 50 GiB free-disk reserve and optional caps. (3) Models loaded by an operation are adopted and keep serving after the control lease ends. (4) Holds of up to 24h exclude a slot from eviction and idle unload. (5) A transition watchdog cancels stalled work. (6) New heartbeat fields report busy reasons, held and adopted models and download usage, only with consent. The visible docs and unit analyses indicate fail-closed design: a closed refusal vocabulary, a local weight-hash recompute before a build joins the set, and adoption ending on consent revocation, unload, hash failure or restart. The T-041 SSD prefix cache, the attestation and App Attest paths (TB-009, TB-011, T-053) and the encryption paths are not visibly touched. I report one low finding: the default-on, uncapped download surface is a disk-fill/availability concern related to T-016 and A-004, and the threat model has no entry for Autopilot downloads or adoption. Unverified, because the code is outside the replay (318 units omitted): ModelDownloader manifest and hash verification on the Autopilot path, the default AutopilotDownloadSettings, ledger file permissions, autopilotServesModel versus autopilotAllowsModel strictness, whether every exit path balances the transitionGenerations.begin calls, hold_seconds clamp enforcement, whether holds can starve ordinary serving (T-029), and whether autopilotHistory detail strings can carry sensitive data. The next pass should read those sources directly.

findings.detail: The changelog (changelog.d/autopilot-placements-and-busy-reasons.md line 5) says that with saved Autopilot consent, Autopilot can download catalog models on the operator's behalf, on by default. The `downloads enable` docs say that blank limits mean no limit. The only default guard is the 50 GiB free-disk reserve. Consent was originally given for selecting models, not for bulk downloads. A misbehaving controller or coordinator could use prefetch_model to fill the model-cache volume down to that reserve. That degrades provider availability and widens the A-004 weight-acquisition surface. Fix: default to bounded max_storage_gb and max_models, or require a separate explicit download opt-in, and add controller-initiated downloads to the threat model. The enforcing code was not in the supplied replay, so the behavior is unverified.
findings.title: Autopilot downloads become default-on for consented Macs with no default storage or model cap
